items.reason: Whole-set setup prints the set identifier, resolved Runtime path, and routed binding kind before the status table.
Header rendering is unconditional in whole-set setup, including inside the bound checkout.
The invocation directory prints only when it differs from the Runtime, accounting for symlinks.
Routing propagates BoundDefault into the header’s binding-recorded announcement.
The old conditional bound-checkout report is removed.
Single-task AFK execution prints the current-checkout path without a Drain header.
The HITL branch returns through runTargetedHITLGate before reaching the new current-checkout line.
Whole-set completion prints one green done result through renderTaskDone.
Both commit SHA and verified no-op details print beneath the done result.
The shared attempt executor no longer prints the old completion line; whole-set endings use mutually exclusive result paths.
Retry exhaustion that fails the task prints one red failed result and preserves the failed transition.
Provider exhaustion preserves the open task and prints one red out-of-agents result instead of failed.
Quota parking prints the yellow quota-paused result with the selected preset before waiting.
Interrupted execution errors produce the yellow interrupted result.
Blocked and Deferred remain set-level reports, while executed tasks receive their own results.
Attempt failures, timing breakdowns, and exhausted-walk narration remain intact.
Both renderers use the existing output layer, preserving full plain text for redirected output.
Result styling uses terminal detection and the existing NO_COLOR suppression.
The new renderers only write output and introduce no journal events.

scores.rationale: Clear rendering helpers and useful tests, but HITL coverage is missing and moving the single-task success summary also falsely announces completion on quota pauses.

accepted.behaviour: A single-task file run of a HITL task also prints that current-checkout line, and prints no Drain header.
accepted.reason: The spec (spec.md:7, 31) says that every single-task file run prints the current-checkout line. In the Reference, a HITL task returns through `runTargetedHITLGate` before `renderCurrentCheckoutLine`, so the line never prints. The spec wins; the Reference misses this behaviour.
